front: What is API design in one sentence?
back: Contract between clients and backend — resource-oriented URLs, predictable errors, auth; hide implementation, not capability.

front: Explain the mental model of API design (how the system thinks).
back: Good API design optimizes for who can call what, how, and what they get back — not for mirroring database tables. URLs express a resource hierarchy; HTTP methods express intent; status codes express outcome. Versioning and pagination are part of the contract from day one, not retrofits.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for API design?
back: Descending specificity: domain → type → entity → action sub-resource. → Offset pagination OK for admin UIs; degrades on large tables (database sharding).

front: Given a broken API design setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Descending specificity: domain → type → entity → action sub-resource.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for API design?
back: Descending specificity: domain → type → entity → action sub-resource.

front: Symptom: 429 storms — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Client retry without backoff · Fix: Exponential backoff + jitter; raise limits if legit

front: Symptom: Duplicate orders — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: POST retried · Fix: Idempotency-Key header + store

front: Symptom: 404 vs empty list — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong path vs filter · Fix: GET /items → [] not 404

front: Symptom: N+1 from mobile — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Chatty fine-grained API · Fix: Aggregate DTO endpoint

front: Symptom: Breaking mobile old app — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Field removed from v1 · Fix: Additive changes only; version bump

front: Symptom: CORS errors browser — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Preflight · Fix: Allow origin + methods; not API "bug"

front: Symptom: Slow list endpoints — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing index on sort column · Fix: DB index; cursor pagination

front: Gotcha with API design: what silently fails?
back: Leaking internal IDs — exposure enables enumeration; use opaque public IDs.

front: When should you NOT use API design?
back: gRPC internal east-west — HTTP JSON for public/partner; gRPC for service mesh if already standard. GraphQL for 3-field mobile screen — complexity tax unless many client shapes. Hypermedia HATEOAS everywhere — rarely pays off for mobile/SPA teams.

front: What is HES Architecture in one sentence?
back: HES acronym is ambiguous in this vault (no prior mentions) — commonly Home Energy System, Head-End System (utilities/AMI), or Health Examination System. Below: high-availability edge service pattern applicable to meter gateways, clinic edge nodes, or IoT aggregators — define your domain acronym in the project README.

front: Explain the mental model of HES Architecture (how the system thinks).
back: HES role: sit at the edge of trust — authenticate devices, normalize payloads, absorb burst traffic, survive upstream outages, never lose acknowledged reads.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for HES Architecture?
back: If your HES = utility head-end: add protocol adapters (DLMS/COSEM, IEC 61850). If health edge: PHI encryption, audit, HIPAA boundary before cloud.

front: Given a broken HES Architecture setup, what is your first validation command?
back: If your HES = utility head-end: add protocol adapters (DLMS/COSEM, IEC 61850). If health edge: PHI encryption, audit, HIPAA boundary before cloud.

front: Symptom: Devices retry storm — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: 5xx rate, timeout · Fix: Scale HES pods; extend adapter backoff; fix DB pool

front: Symptom: Duplicate readings in billing — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Idempotency key · Fix: Enforce (device_id, seq) unique; audit adapter gen

front: Symptom: Edge disk full — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Spool PVC usage · Fix: Increase retention policy; restore WAN; drop policy w/ audit

front: Symptom: Auth failures spike — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cert rotation · Fix: Push new device certs; check clock skew (NTP)

front: Symptom: Cloud sees gaps — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: forward_lag metric · Fix: Network partition — expected; backfill from spool

front: Symptom: Latency SLO miss — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Hot partition device · Fix: Shard by deviceId; async pipeline

front: Symptom: "HES" means different thing per team — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Glossary · Fix: Rename service in docs; link domain spec

front: Gotcha with HES Architecture: what silently fails?
back: At-least-once everywhere — without idempotent core, duplicates become revenue or clinical errors.

front: When should you NOT use HES Architecture?
back: Direct device-to-cloud only — no outage buffer; fine for low-value telemetry, not billing/medical grade. Monolith ingest in single VM — first WAN blip becomes data loss without queue. Custom binary protocol without schema registry — versioning hell at 10k firmware variants.

front: What is KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) in one sentence?
back: Prefer the simplest design that meets requirements — complexity is a liability with compound interest.

front: Explain the mental model of KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) (how the system thinks).
back: KISS pushes teams to choose understandable solutions over clever ones. Every abstraction, service boundary, and config flag has operational cost — on-call must debug it at 3 AM. Simple code is easier to read, test, change, and delete; complexity hides bugs and slows onboarding.

front: What is Splitwise in one sentence?
back: Expense-sharing system design — groups, balances, debt simplification, notifications; classic interview + real fintech patterns.

front: Explain the mental model of Splitwise (how the system thinks).
back: Splitwise-like apps track who paid and who owes whom in groups. Core insight: store atomic expenses (who paid, split among whom) then derive balances; optionally simplify debts so A→B→C becomes A→C. Not a payment processor — ledger + settlement tracking unless integrated with Stripe/UPI.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Splitwise?

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Splitwise?
back: Store money as integer cents — never float (marshalling lesson).

front: Symptom: Split sum ≠ expense — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: User sees other group — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Duplicate expenses — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Simplify confuses users — what do you check and fix?

front: When should you NOT use Splitwise?
back: Enterprise AP/AR — use real accounting ERP; tax/invoicing rules differ. High-frequency trading ledger — different consistency/latency model. Single-user budget app — no group balance graph needed.

front: What is Cache system in one sentence?
back: Fast read path in front of slow/expensive source — TTL, invalidation, and stampede control define correctness.

front: Explain the mental model of Cache system (how the system thinks).
back: A cache stores copies of data closer to readers (memory, edge, CDN) to cut latency and load on origin (DB, API). Caches are eventually consistent by definition — the hard part is when to expire and how to invalidate without thundering herds.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Cache system?
back: Never Cache-Control: public on personalized JSON without Vary: Authorization review.

front: Given a broken Cache system setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Never Cache-Control: public on personalized JSON without Vary: Authorization review.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Cache system?
back: Never Cache-Control: public on personalized JSON without Vary: Authorization review.

front: Symptom: Stale data after update — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: TTL only, no invalidation · Fix: Delete key on write; shorter TTL

front: Symptom: Redis OOM — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: INFO memory; evictions · Fix: Raise maxmemory; LRU policy; smaller values

front: Symptom: Thundering herd on expiry — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Spike on DB at T+0 · Fix: Jitter TTL; singleflight rebuild

front: Symptom: "Random" DNS failures — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: resolvectl statistics · Fix: Flush cache; fix authoritative NS

front: Symptom: CDN serves old API — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong Cache-Control · Fix: private/no-store on auth responses

front: Symptom: Cache hit rate 0 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Key churn / wrong prefix · Fix: Namespace keys; log miss reason

front: Symptom: Inconsistent replicas — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Read from replica lag · Fix: Read-your-writes: primary or version check

front: Gotcha with Cache system: what silently fails?
back: Cache null results — cache "user not found" with short TTL or attackers/bugs hammer DB.

front: When should you NOT use Cache system?
back: Strong consistency required — read from primary or use linearizable store; no silent cache. Write-heavy counters — aggregate in DB/Redis INCR, not read-modify-write cache loop. Secrets — don't cache API keys in CDN edge.

back: Churn rate (attrition) measures how many customers stop paying or actively leave in a time window, expressed as a percentage of the starting cohort. It is the inverse lens of retention: high churn destroys unit economics and leaves orphaned data, idle seats, and over-provisioned capacity.

front: What is Database sharding in one sentence?
back: Split one logical database into independent shards — horizontal scale when single-node limits hit, not day-one default.

front: Explain the mental model of Database sharding (how the system thinks).
back: Sharding partitions rows across multiple databases by a shard key (user_id, tenant_id, geo). Each shard holds a subset of data; the application routes queries to the correct shard(s). Cross-shard joins and transactions become expensive or impossible — design around shard-local access patterns.

front: Symptom: Cross-shard timeout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Scatter-gather query · Fix: Redesign schema; denormalize

front: Symptom: User on wrong shard — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Routing bug · Fix: Consistent hash; migration table

front: Symptom: Replica lag read stale — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Read from replica · Fix: Read-your-writes from primary

front: Symptom: Transaction fails across shards — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: 2PC not used · Fix: Saga / outbox pattern

front: Symptom: Backup uneven — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: One huge shard · Fix: Rebalance

front: Symptom: Connection pool exhaustion — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Per-shard pools · Fix: Size pools × shard count

front: Gotcha with Database sharding: what silently fails?
back: Shard too early — operational complexity kills team; exhaust vertical scale + replicas first.

front: When should you NOT use Database sharding?
back: < 100 GB with low QPS — single Postgres + replicas sufficient. Heavy cross-entity analytics — warehouse (OLAP) not OLTP shard. Strong global transactions — shard fights ACID across boundaries.

front: What is Marshalling in one sentence?
back: Convert in-memory structures ↔ wire/storage bytes across process boundaries — schema + version discipline prevent silent corruption.

front: Explain the mental model of Marshalling (how the system thinks).
back: Marshalling (synonymous with serialization in most teams) transforms runtime objects into bytes for network, disk, or IPC, and unmarshals back on the receiver. Boundaries: different languages, different processes, different versions — all need an explicit format contract.

front: Symptom: Garbled strings — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: UTF-8 vs Latin-1 · Fix: Enforce UTF-8; Content-Type charset

front: Symptom: Works Java, fails Go — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: JSON field casing · Fix: Tag conventions; shared OpenAPI

front: Symptom: Old client crash on deploy — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: New required field · Fix: Optional fields + defaults

front: Symptom: Float rounding — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: JSON number precision · Fix: Use string decimal or int cents

front: Symptom: Huge payloads — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Marshal entire graph · Fix: DTO projection; pagination

front: Symptom: Kafka poison message — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Bad Avro schema ID · Fix: Schema registry; DLQ

front: Symptom: Endian binary bug — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Raw struct pack · Fix: Use protobuf, not manual pack

front: Gotcha with Marshalling: what silently fails?
back: Marshal same object graph twice — circular references blow JSON serializers.

front: When should you NOT use Marshalling?
back: Same process, same language — pass object references; no marshal. Shared memory ring buffer — fixed binary layout OK with strict schema doc. JSON for high-frequency numeric telemetry — protobuf/MessagePack bandwidth.

front: What is Server in one sentence?
back: Long-lived process accepting client requests — connection model + state strategy define scale and failure modes.

front: Explain the mental model of Server (how the system thinks).
back: A server listens on a port, accepts connections or requests, executes handlers, returns responses. Design choices: thread vs event loop, stateless vs session, HTTP vs WebSocket/SSE. Scale = many concurrent connections without exhausting file descriptors or memory (concurrent connection).

back: Check: Process down; wrong port · Fix: systemd status; bind 0.0.0.0

front: Symptom: 502 from LB — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Slow under load — what do you check and fix?

front: Gotcha with Server: what silently fails?

front: When should you NOT use Server?
back: Pure static site — object storage + CDN, no app server. Heavy GPU transcode — worker process, not HTTP request thread (Encoding). Long batch ETL — job queue worker, not synchronous HTTP server.

front: What is Stateless offset handling in one sentence?
back: Kafka consumer offset patterns for "stateless" services — commits, rebalance, duplicates, and exactly-once illusions — Kleppmann / Kafka ops canon.

front: Explain the mental model of Stateless offset handling (how the system thinks).
back: A consumer's offset is its cursor in a partition log. Stateless here means: no durable local DB for progress — the broker (or coordinator) stores committed offsets in __consumer_offsets. On restart/rebalance, processing resumes from last commit.

front: Symptom: Consumer kicked from group — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: max.poll.interval exceeded · Fix: Smaller batches; async process + pause; scale consumers

front: Symptom: Message storm duplicates — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Recent deploy before commit · Fix: Idempotent handler; dedupe store

front: Symptom: Lag growing — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: RECORDS-LAG-MAX; slow process · Fix: Scale partitions/consumers; optimize handler

front: Symptom: Lost messages — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: auto.commit=true · Fix: Disable auto commit; commit after success

front: Symptom: Rebalance loop — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Processing > session.timeout · Fix: Tune timeouts; static membership group.instance.id

front: Symptom: Offset reset surprise — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: auto.offset.reset=latest new group · Fix: Explicit reset policy; document consumer group naming

front: Symptom: "Exactly-once" but double DB rows — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Side effect outside TX · Fix: Idempotent-key or outbox

front: Gotcha with Stateless offset handling: what silently fails?
back: Commit then crash before process — at-most-once gap if you reversed order wrong.

front: When should you NOT use Stateless offset handling?
back: Commit-before-process for money movement — unacceptable loss window. Offset reset in prod without replay capacity — can DDoS your own DB. Kafka transactions to fix non-idempotent HTTP webhooks — fix the handler instead.
